title: docs(pm-dispatch): fold the 2026-08-08/09 shift's measured lessons in — 7 added/merged, 2 dropped as already covered (#6902)
body:
Fixes #6902

Folds the shift's measured lessons into `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`. **+148 / −5 lines, one file** (`git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`).

The card carries **eight** numbered lessons plus a **ninth** in its own comments (the 03:35Z maintainer ruling that superseded the 03:31Z draft). The ninth is treated as in scope: it is a maintainer ruling recorded on this card, and this file's own step 1 says a ruling that lives only in a comment is a ruling the next reader skips.

Branch cut from `main` at `6dd3c251b`, i.e. **after** all five of tonight's SKILL merges — #6871 (dispatch-model economics), #6886 (domain vocabulary), #6959, #6911 and #6974. The dispatch order named two; the log named five, so the whole file was re-read before writing rather than diffed against the two.

## Disposition of every entry — added / merged / dropped

| # | Entry | Disposition | Where it landed, and why there |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Push branch, open draft PR, then wait for CI — as a fixed dispatch clause | **Merged (one paragraph), and the card's prescription deliberately NOT followed** | Both halves already existed: the producer-side ordering is `os-dev.md`'s Definition of done (push → draft PR → CI convergence → report), and the PM-side "report lost ≠ acceptance stalled" path is step 6 with its three conditions and the #5550/#5556 precedent. Writing it into the dispatch order as the card asks would **contradict #6871**, which sank unconditional clauses into `os-dev.md` precisely so prompts carry deltas only. What was genuinely new is the *reason*, so that is what landed: a paragraph in step 6 recording that the death cause can be **fleet-wide** (two account-wide token exhaustions, four in-flight devs each time), that in that cell the probe half is unavailable too so only conditions (a) and (c) are readable, and that the four cards lost zero information because the PR was already up. It says explicitly that this does **not** license copying the ordering into prompts. |
| 2 | File surface must say "expected landing site + what to do when the producer is in another package" | **Added** — step 5, immediately under the ruling/assumption partition | A dispatch order naming one path asks the dev to choose between keeping its word and fixing the right thing — and `os-dev.md` rule 5 (contract-first) already binds it to the second. Both paths verified present on `main`: consumer `packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts`, producer `packages/spec/src/data/context-tokens.zod.ts`. Added the mechanical fact the card leaves implicit: **cross-package usually means cross-lane** here (#5586 is labeled `domain:engine-core`; `packages/spec` is permanently the spec seat's under "shared contract surfaces have one owner"), so the route is rule 4's existing cross-seat machinery plus the after-the-fact declaration (#6532 precedent, #6017) — no new mechanism minted. |
| 3 | Closing/voiding on someone else's instruction needs a provenance comment | **Added** — State model, label discipline | The neighbouring bullets bind a state change to its paired record; none binds it to its **reason**, and a closure's reason cannot be read back out of the state machine. Correction relayed: **#6668 is a PR, not an issue** (draft ADR-0123, closed unmerged 2026-08-08 13:54Z) — `issue_read get_labels` cannot even resolve it. The new bullet points at the Guardrails ADR clause that already cites the same PR, so a reader does not think there are two #6668 stories: that one records the **decision**, this one the **execution record**. |
| 4 | Enumerate the gate list on the spot, never from memory | **Merged** — step 5, next to the template's local-gate line | Both trigger events verified in today's tree: `check:kernel-hook-pairs` at `lint.yml:551` (#6672) and `check:app-nav-i18n` at `lint.yml:1219` (#6661). **The card's prescription needed correcting before relaying:** "enumerate from `.github/workflows/lint.yml`" is itself memory-shaped — measured today, 61 `pnpm check:*` invocations are in `lint.yml` and **7 are not** (`ci.yml`, `spec-liveness-check.yml`, `validate-deps.yml`, `release.yml`, `showcase-smoke.yml`). So the paragraph gives a command across all workflows instead of a filename, and folds in the dispatching seat's matching finding (#6865: four of six relayed required-context names live in `ci.yml`) and #6673 (a relayed line number that landed in a different function). It also states the boundary #6871 created: **the PM takes the reading, not the dev** — devs no longer run the farm locally, so the accuracy of naming is now the PM's alone. |
| 5 | Alternative discipline when the maintainer exempts same-file serialization | **Added** — step 3, directly under the "no exception" paragraph | Placed there because that paragraph currently reads as absolute; an exemption written anywhere else would read as a contradiction. Discipline ① (region-level declaration) is cross-referenced to the seat post's hot-file serial queue rather than restated, with the division of labour named: that section records the standing cross-round order, this one the current round's disjointness proof. Guardrails' "file-disjoint by construction" bullet gained a one-clause pointer for the same reason. |
| 6 | PM mechanism assumptions must be marked "measure this, falsification encouraged" | **Dropped as already covered — but its gap was fixed** | The rule exists three times over: step 5's ruling/assumption partition with three same-day falsifications, step 3's unlock paragraph, step 7's "acknowledge it in the open". Restating it would be the fourth. What measurement showed was a **third category neither block covers**: an option the PM merely *suggests*. Both of tonight's overturns were that shape — #6865's asked-for "no `if:`" assertion would have reddened four correct jobs, and #6893's dispatch offered excluding `content/docs/releases/**` as defensible when that is #4920's rejected option A. Verified rather than relayed: `scripts/docs-audit/check-audit-scope.mjs` calls `process.exit(1)` when no release page remains in scope, and its comments name #4920 and #6893 by number. So the partition became **three blocks** — in the prose, in the prompt template, and in the bullet above the template, all in one pass, since a template disagreeing with its own explanation is the drift this file keeps paying for. |
| 7 | Cloud cards must be archived after merge | **Merged** — landing section B, into the existing unsubscribe rule | `archive_session` appeared **nowhere** in the file before this. It fires on the same event as the unsubscribe that was already written there, so it belongs in that sentence rather than in a new paragraph or in the backends section: the trigger is the **card's terminal state** (PR MERGED or card voided), not "the dev reported". Cost kept: 11 finished-but-unarchived idle containers, which do not error, do not occupy the queue, and show on no board. |
| 8 | Split cards inherit the parent's release label | **Added** — release board, right under the binary criterion | Placed under the criterion because the honest rule is "re-run the criterion on each half", not "copy the label". #6806 was verified in both directions and it is a specimen of both: its body argues **"why `pm:queue` without `target:v17`"** using the four blocking classes, and that reasoning was later re-judged — today #6806 and #5495 both carry `target:v17`. The rule therefore reads: default is inheritance (the obligation follows the work), and a half judged not to inherit must argue it **on the card in the four-class terms**, falsifiably. Producer discipline unchanged. |
| 9 | Wave rhythm: finish a wave, archive, compact, continue (03:35Z ruling, superseding the 03:31Z rotation draft) | **Added** — step 9, after the round-report metrics | The wave boundary is where the round loop already ends, so a reader looking for "what happens between waves" looks there. Records the cost reading that drove the ruling (`cache_read` 10.18M against 6.9K uncached input on a ~2h cloud card), the four ordered steps, and the two boundaries the ruling itself draws: seat rotation demoted to an end-of-shift action because compaction **preserves session bindings** (PR subscriptions, self-bound `send_later` timers, the seat post's session ID, cloud-card parentage), and **Routine seats are exempt** since each fire rebuilds from GitHub. Step 2 of the four is explicitly framed as settling an existing debt ("state changes do not sleep over"), not a new obligation. |

Two entries from the dispatching seat's own shift notes rode along, both as **merges into rules they sharpen**, not as new rules:

- **Probe escalation gained a middle rung.** The stalled-subagent rules said restate the posture, then declare unreliable on the third stall. Measured this shift: three devs ended their turn waiting on timers they had armed themselves; two recovered on a first probe that named the mechanism, and the third **repeated the same stall immediately after being told** — recovery needed a probe naming the exact next tool call and forbidding background waits outright. The ladder is now ① restate posture → ② name the next tool call + forbid background waits → ③ unreliable, with the point that re-sending ① verbatim is not a reset yet still spends one of the three counts.
- **Re-verify relayed line-level claims** — merged into entry 4's paragraph rather than given its own, since it is the same discipline as #6413, #6492 and the compile-surface table's existing warning; the paragraph names all four positions so the next reader does not re-derive them.

## Verification — stated plainly, because the honest answer is unusual here

**Skill prose is not asserted by any test in this repo.** There is no before-red/after-green artifact to produce for a documentation sentence, and manufacturing one would be worse than saying so. What *is* verifiable was run, and what the card claimed was measured rather than transcribed.

Gates, all green in the worktree (every gate whose script reads `.claude/**`, found by `grep -rln "\.claude" scripts/*.mjs`):

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `check:nul-bytes` | 6500 tracked text files, no raw ASCII control bytes |
| `check:skill-frame-sync` | 12 self-test cases pass; 4 isomorphic frame copies across 3 files, 4 count mentions agree, 42 markdown files scanned for undeclared copies |
| `check:skill-frame-freshness` | 12 self-test cases pass; frame current with `origin/main` (fetched at run time) |
| `check:skill-compatibility` | 18 self-test cases pass; 11 SKILL.md files reconciled against 77 workspace packages |
| `check:doc-authoring` | self-test passes (scope wiring confirms `.claude` is in scope); 374 files clean |
| `check:agent-model-declared` | 18 self-test cases pass (run because the diff cites `os-dev.md`; that file is untouched) |

Also run: `grep -naP` over the changed file for the full control-byte class beyond NUL — clean. `check:skill-examples` is not applicable: this file carries no `os:check` blocks.

**Contradiction sweep** — the whole file was re-read against the additions, and three collisions were resolved in the edit rather than left for a reader:

1. The card asks for a fixed push/PR/CI clause in the dispatch order; #6871 sank unconditional clauses out of prompts. Resolved by landing the *reading*, not the clause, and saying so in the text.
2. The card asks the dispatch order to say "enumerate from `lint.yml`"; #6871 forbids the dev enumerating the farm locally. Resolved by making the PM the party who takes the reading.
3. Entry 5's exemption path vs. Guardrails' "file-disjoint by construction". Resolved with a one-clause pointer in Guardrails so the two rules agree instead of merely coexisting.

**Numbering discipline observed**: no Operational note was added or renumbered. Every entry landed inside an existing section next to the rule it modifies, which is what keeps the numbered ledger stable.

## Not merged by an AI seat

This PR governs the PM seat's own behaviour, so self-review-and-merge is prohibited — it is held for the maintainer, and no auto-merge is armed. `docs/adr/**` and `content/docs/releases/**` are untouched. `.claude/`-only ⇒ no changeset; `skip-changeset` applied by the author with the label set read back after the bots settled.
